questions.stem: How does Network Data Modelling organise data?
options: Using owner–member sets that allow records to participate in multiple parent and child relationships
Using a strict tree in which each child has exactly one parent
Using fact tables surrounded by dimension tables
Using JSON documents with embedded arrays
Using classes with attributes and methods
questions.explanation: The network model uses owner–member sets, forming a flexible graph-like structure where records can have many-to-many connections.

questions.stem: What limitation of hierarchical databases was the network model designed to overcome?
options: The lack of atomic values
The restriction that each child could have only one parent
The absence of primary keys
The inability to store repayment history
The need for declarative queries
questions.explanation: In hierarchical systems each child could have only one parent, making many-to-many relationships hard to represent; the network model removed that restriction.

questions.stem: Through which group and system did the network model gain prominence in the 1960s?
options: ODMG and ObjectStore
IBM and IMS
The CODASYL Data Base Task Group and IDMS
W3C and RDF
Apache and Cassandra
questions.explanation: The network model gained prominence through the CODASYL Data Base Task Group and systems such as IDMS, used widely in banking, insurance and government.

questions.stem: In the network model loan example, which relationship is described as many-to-many?
options: Customer → LoanApplication
LoanApplication → Branch
LoanApplication → Repayment
LoanApplication → LoanOfficer
Branch → Customer
questions.explanation: A LoanApplication can be reviewed by multiple LoanOfficers and each LoanOfficer can handle multiple LoanApplications, a many-to-many link that hierarchical trees could not express.

questions.stem: What kind of querying does the network model require?
options: Declarative SQL queries
Semantic reasoning over classes and rules
Full-text search
Map-reduce aggregation
Navigational querying in which developers explicitly define how to traverse from record to record
questions.explanation: Unlike relational SQL, which declares what result is needed, the network model forces the application to specify how to reach the data through procedural traversal.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a weakness of network data modelling?
options: Inability to represent many-to-many relationships
Requirement for procedural navigation that makes ad-hoc analysis difficult
Schema changes rippling into application logic
Lack of the mathematical foundation provided by relational databases
Lack of relational abstraction
questions.explanation: Support for many-to-many relationships is a strength of the network model, not a weakness; its weaknesses concern procedural navigation, coupling and missing theoretical foundation.

questions.stem: Which modern technology carries on the network model's idea of interconnected records?
options: Star schema data warehouses
Graph databases
Key–value caches
Columnar analytical stores
Object-relational mapping frameworks
questions.explanation: The conceptual idea of interconnected records lives on in modern graph databases, making the network model an early ancestor of graph-based modelling.

questions.stem: What is the core difference between the network model and an ontology?
options: The network model is drawn as a tree while an ontology is drawn as a graph
The network model is a modern AI technique while an ontology is a 1960s storage technique
The network model is a storage technique using physical pointers, whereas an ontology is a knowledge representation model focused on meaning and reasoning
The network model uses SQL while an ontology uses procedural code
They differ only in the vendors that support them
questions.explanation: The network model organises data records through pointers; an ontology, expressed in standards such as OWL or RDF, organises knowledge and supports logical reasoning.

questions.stem: How do queries in ontology-based systems differ from queries in the network model?
options: Ontology queries must specify the traversal path explicitly
Ontology queries are limited to a single parent–child level
Ontology queries require physical pointers between records
Ontology queries are declarative and semantic, using reasoning over classes, properties and rules rather than a traversal path
Ontology queries can only return counts
questions.explanation: In an ontology a user asks a semantic question such as which officers approved loans for high-risk customers, and the system reasons over defined classes and rules rather than navigating links.

questions.stem: Which statement about semantics in the network model is correct?
options: The network model defines relationships such as Loan is_a FinancialAgreement
The network model can infer new facts from class definitions
The network model automatically classifies high-risk loans
The network model encodes inheritance hierarchies
The network model has no inherent semantic understanding; it stores and traverses links without knowing what a Customer or Loan represents
questions.explanation: The network model connects records through pointers but does not know what those records mean; encoding meaning and inference is the role of ontologies.
